com.vector.cfg.dom.modemgt.groovy.bswm

Interface IBswMAutoConfigurationApi

  • All Superinterfaces:
    IBswMAutoConfigurationDomain, IBswMAutoConfigurationElement

    @PublishedApi(value=ADDITIONS_ALLOWED)
 @PublishedApiDomain(value=AUTOMATION_IF)
public interface IBswMAutoConfigurationApi
extends IBswMAutoConfigurationDomain
    IBswMAutoConfigurationApi allows for automatic creation of dedicated parts of the BswM configuration.
    The IBswMAutoConfigurationApi allows for semi-automatic creation of dedicated parts of the BswM configuration. The BswM auto configuration takes an input consisting of "features" and "parameters" to be provided via the IBswMAutoConfigurationApi. Each feature may have zero, one or more sub-features and zero, one or more parameters.

    The corresponding BswM configuration content is derived based on the (de)activation of features and the values assigned to the parameters.

    The available features and parameters depend strongly on the project's input data and general project setup. They can be addressed by String identifiers. These identifiers are best obtained from the corresponding auto configuration assistant of the BSW management editor in the Cfg5 GUI.

    • Method Detail

      • activate

        @PublishedMethod
void activate(java.lang.String featureId)
        activate(String) activates the BswM auto configuration feature with the given identifier.
        Activating BswM Auto Configuration Features
        activate(String) activates the BswM auto configuration feature with the given identifier. All enabled sub-features of the specified feature are also activated. Imagine the features displayed in a tree structure (like in Cfg5 GUI) where checking a tree node automatically checks all children.
        Throws:
        java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if there is no feature with the given identifier
        java.lang.IllegalStateException - if the feature with the given identifier is disabled

      • deactivate

        @PublishedMethod
void deactivate(java.lang.String featureId)
        deactivate(String) deactivates the BswM auto configuration feature with the given identifier.
        Deactivating BswM Auto Configuration Features
        deactivate(String) deactivates the BswM auto configuration feature with the given identifier. All enabled sub-features of the specified feature are also deactivated. Imagine the features displayed in a tree structure (like in Cfg5 GUI) where unchecking a tree node automatically unchecks all children.
        Throws:
        java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if there is no feature with the given identifier
        java.lang.IllegalStateException - if the feature with the given identifier is disabled

      • overrides

        @PublishedMethod
void overrides(@VDelegatesToWithClosureParam(value=IBswMAutoConfigurationOverride.class)
                                 groovy.lang.Closure<?> callback)
        Using overrides(Closure) a callback can be registered for deciding how to handle manual adaptations of the auto-generated configuration content.
        Manually Adapting the BswM Auto Configuration Content
        The BswM auto configuration mechanism is useful for creating large parts of the BswM configuration based on certain built-in heuristics. Where these heuristics fail to fulfill detailed project specific requirements manual adaptations to the auto-generated configuration content become necessary.

        Per default manual adjustments are kept in the configuration. But subsequent BswM auto configuration runs may render previously applied adjustments obsolete or dysfunctional. Using overrides(Closure) a callback can be registered to be called for each detected adaptation. The callback can decide for each adjustment if it is to remain in the configuration or if it is to be overwritten by the BswM auto configuration. For details on which information is provided to this callback please refer to the javadoc provided with IBswMAutoConfigurationOverride.

      • set

        @PublishedMethod
IBswMAutoConfigurationParameterSetter set(java.lang.String parameterId)
        set(String) sets the parameter with the given identifier to the specified value.
        Assigning Values to BswM Auto Configuration Parameters
        set(String) sets the parameter with the given identifier to the specified value. Supported value types are boolean, BigInteger, BigDecimal, String and MIReferrable (reference parameters).
        Throws:
        java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if there is no parameter with the given identifier
        java.lang.IllegalStateException - if the parameter with the given identifier is disabled
